entries.definition: a defined set of steps for solving a problem
entries.example: The algorithm sorts the records by date before displaying them.

entries.definition: the use of systems to carry out tasks with less direct human action
entries.example: Automation reduced repeated typing but did not remove the need for checking.

entries.definition: computer methods designed to perform tasks associated with human intelligence
entries.example: The workshop examines how artificial intelligence can assist with writing.

entries.definition: the controls and display through which someone uses a program
entries.example: The interface makes the save button easy to find.

entries.definition: the basic equipment and systems needed for an activity
entries.example: Reliable digital infrastructure matters when a service must stay available.

entries.definition: an organized collection of information stored for retrieval
entries.example: The database keeps article progress separate from the article text.

entries.definition: changing data into a protected form readable with the proper key
entries.example: Encryption helps protect private information during transmission.

entries.definition: checking that a person or system is who it claims to be
entries.example: Authentication happens before the system opens the private account.

entries.definition: deciding what an identified user or system may access
entries.example: Authorization limits which records each staff member can change.

entries.definition: a weakness that could allow harm or unwanted access
entries.example: The update repairs a vulnerability in the old component.

entries.definition: a method that takes advantage of a security weakness
entries.example: The team fixed the weakness before a known exploit could affect users.

entries.definition: a small software change that fixes a specific problem
entries.example: The patch corrects the error without replacing the whole application.

entries.definition: the ability of systems or parts to work together
entries.example: We checked compatibility with older devices before publishing the update.

entries.definition: to arrange settings so a system works as intended
entries.example: Please configure the printer before sending the final document.

entries.definition: to change something to suit a particular user or need
entries.example: Readers can customize the text size without changing the article.

entries.definition: to make related information or processes agree in time or content
entries.example: The devices synchronize their calendars when a connection becomes available.

entries.definition: the amount of data a connection can carry in a given time
entries.example: The audio version requires less bandwidth than the video stream.

entries.definition: the delay between an action and its response in a system
entries.example: High latency made the conversation feel less natural.

entries.definition: the maximum amount a system can hold or handle
entries.example: The storage capacity must cover both recordings and backups.

entries.definition: to improve a system for a particular purpose or limit
entries.example: The developer will optimize the query after measuring its performance.

entries.definition: achieving useful results with little wasted time or resources
entries.example: The efficient search avoids loading every record at once.

entries.definition: the ability to handle growth without unacceptable loss of performance
entries.example: The team tested scalability with a much larger set of records.

entries.definition: a period when a service or supply stops working
entries.example: The internet outage did not prevent access to saved articles.

entries.definition: an interruption that prevents normal activity
entries.example: The team planned the update to minimize disruption for learners.

entries.definition: the process of returning data or a system to a usable state
entries.example: A separate copy made recovery possible after the failed update.

entries.definition: the completeness and consistency of stored or transferred data
entries.example: The verification step checks the integrity of the backup.

entries.definition: a calculated value used to help detect changes in data
entries.example: The checksum changed after one byte of the file was altered.

entries.definition: software designed to harm systems or misuse information
entries.example: The training explains why unknown attachments may contain malware.

entries.definition: deceptive messages intended to steal private information
entries.example: The phishing email copied the appearance of a familiar service.

entries.definition: deliberate deception intended to gain money or another advantage
entries.example: The payment team investigated the report of online fraud.

entries.definition: permission given freely after understanding what is involved
entries.example: The app asks for consent before sending selected text online.

entries.definition: the setting used unless another option is chosen
entries.example: The default keeps downloaded lessons available offline.

entries.definition: available to choose but not required
entries.example: The optional audio exercise does not replace the reading task.

entries.definition: required by a rule or necessary procedure
entries.example: A mandatory check prevents incomplete backups from being accepted.

entries.definition: easy to carry or move between suitable systems
entries.example: The portable recorder fits inside a small shoulder bag.

entries.definition: created or provided through computer systems rather than a physical setting
entries.example: The virtual classroom connects learners in different cities.

entries.definition: allowing a user to respond and influence what happens
entries.example: The interactive diagram changes when students select a different value.

entries.definition: responding smoothly or adapting appropriately to user actions or screen size
entries.example: A responsive layout keeps buttons usable on a small screen.

entries.definition: to find your way through a system or place
entries.example: Clear headings help readers navigate the digital library.

entries.definition: to find and bring back stored information
entries.example: The search can retrieve an article by its title.

entries.definition: to store information that is not needed for current work
entries.example: We archive completed projects without deleting their records.

entries.definition: an extra copy of an existing item
entries.example: The system found a duplicate before adding another review card.

entries.definition: a particular form of something that has been changed over time
entries.example: Each version includes a clear record of its changes.

entries.definition: an early model used to explore or test a design
entries.example: The prototype used paper screens before any code was written.

entries.definition: to make a prepared system available for real use
entries.example: The team will deploy the update after the safety checks pass.

entries.definition: to keep something working properly over time
entries.example: Small regular checks help maintain the equipment.

entries.definition: to observe and record the condition of something over time
entries.example: We monitor the backup process for incomplete files.

entries.definition: to identify the cause of a problem through examination
entries.example: The error report helped us diagnose the failed import.

entries.definition: to find and solve faults in a system
entries.example: The guide shows users how to troubleshoot a missing audio file.

entries.definition: to model a situation so its behavior can be studied
entries.example: The test can simulate a network interruption without contacting a real provider.
